result.description:
La Riviera Dining
Wine & Dine Australia Pty Ltd, trading as Bambini Trust Restaurant
Sydney NSW 2000

Café or Restaurant Manager
Full Time Role
Salary Range $77,000 to $80,000 per annum, plus superannuation.

Key Duties and Responsibilities
1. Operational Management
•	Coordinate daily front-of-house operations, including service setup, staff briefings, and shift supervision. 
•	Ensure smooth collaboration between front-of-house and kitchen teams. 
•	Maintain service standards consistent with the La Riviera brand. 
•	Monitor and improve operational procedures to ensure efficient restaurant operations and high levels of customer satisfaction. 
2. Staff Leadership and Development
•	Coordinate staff recruitment, onboarding and performance management processes. 
•	Plan and deliver training programs focused on guest service, product knowledge and teamwork. 
•	Contribute to building a positive and high-performing workplace culture. 
•	Prepare staff rosters and supervise staff to ensure adequate staffing levels during operating hours. 
3. Guest Experience and Customer Service
•	Manage reservations, guest interactions and special requests. 
•	Handle feedback and complaints with professionalism and discretion. 
•	Participate in the delivery of VIP and high-profile guest experiences. 
•	Monitor customer feedback and implement service improvements to enhance the overall guest experience. 
4. Wine Room and Beverage Coordination
•	Work alongside the Sommelier to oversee wine service, pairing and cellar management. 
•	Coordinate wine and beverage training for staff. 
•	Manage inventory checks and beverage ordering. 
•	Monitor beverage stock levels and ensure appropriate inventory control procedures are maintained. 
5. Financial and Administrative Support
•	Monitor sales performance and implement cost control measures. 
•	Oversee the use of point-of-sale and booking systems. 
•	Manage back-office administrative functions, including timesheet collection and supplier invoicing. 
•	Assist in preparing operational reports and monitoring labour costs to support business profitability. 
6. Compliance and Workplace Safety
•	Ensure compliance with NSW food safety and liquor licensing laws. 
•	Conduct risk assessments and implement workplace health and safety initiatives. 
•	Ensure safe service practices are followed during operations and events. 
•	Monitor compliance with company policies and relevant legislative requirements. 
7. Supplier and Inventory Management
•	Manage stock ordering, deliveries and supplier communications. 
•	Conduct regular stocktakes and identify opportunities to minimise waste. 
•	Ensure quality control of incoming goods and supplies. 
•	Maintain appropriate stock levels to support uninterrupted restaurant operations. 
8. Events and Marketing Support
•	Contribute to the planning and execution of events, such as private dinners and cocktail functions. 
•	Coordinate the promotion of wine tastings, seasonal menus and customer engagement activities. 
•	Monitor customer feedback and participate in continuous improvement discussions. 
•	Work with management to implement promotional initiatives that enhance customer engagement and increase revenue. 


Qualifications
•	A relevant qualification in Hospitality Management, Restaurant Management, Business Management or a related field (such as an AQF Certificate IV, Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Hospitality Management) is desirable. 
•	Alternatively, at least three years of relevant full-time industry experience in restaurant or hospitality management may substitute for formal qualifications, where applicable. 
•	Current Food Safety Supervisor Certificate (or the ability to obtain one). 
•	Current Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) Certificate. 
•	First Aid Certificate is desirable. 

Work Experience
•	At least two years of full-time experience in a managerial role, or three years of relevant experience, in a café, restaurant or similar hospitality establishment. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing the day-to-day operations of a restaurant or café, including front-of-house operations. 
•	Experience recruiting, supervising, training and managing the performance of staff. 
•	Experience managing customer service, resolving guest complaints and maintaining high service standards. 
•	Experience preparing staff rosters, managing inventory, ordering supplies and maintaining stock control. 
•	Experience monitoring food quality, operational efficiency and compliance with food safety and workplace health and safety requirements. 
•	Experience monitoring budgets, labour costs, sales performance and implementing cost control measures. 
•	Experience coordinating private functions, special events or promotional activities is desirable. 
•	Sound knowledge of Australian hospitality legislation, food safety standards and liquor licensing requirements.


How to apply:
Applications open on 21 July 2026 and close on 20 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Unaccredited Trainee - Orthopaedics - Maitland Hospital

Employment Type: Temporary Full Time
Remuneration: $117,745K - $147,664K
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM29879

Build your pathway to Orthopaedic SET with Hunter New England LHD

Maitland Hospital is seeking motivated and career-focused unaccredited trainees to join our Orthopaedic Surgery team.

This role is ideal for doctors intending to pursue Orthopaedic SET training, offering the clinical exposure, mentorship and portfolio development needed to progress to the next stage of your surgical career.

What you'll be doing

Deliver high-quality, patient-centred care within a multidisciplinary orthopaedic team

Actively participate in operating theatre, fracture clinic, and acute orthopaedic care

Develop core orthopaedic knowledge and early procedural capability

Contribute to audit, teaching, and quality improvement activities

Work under close supervision with regular feedback from consultants and senior trainees

SET-focused opportunities

Meaningful theatre exposure with opportunities to assist and build technical confidence

Access to engaged consultants who support trainees progressing to SET

Opportunities to secure strong clinical referees

Participation in audit and quality improvement projects aligned with RACS CV domains

Involvement in teaching and departmental education sessions

Experience that supports development of a competitive SET application portfolio

What we can offer you

A supportive and inclusive team with a strong focus on education, supervision and wellbeing

Hands-on experience across a diverse mix of elective and acute orthopaedic presentations

Dedicated opportunities to strengthen your clinical, academic and professional profile

A modern, well-equipped facility within a progressive health district

Why Maitland?

Maitland Hospital is a key regional facility within Hunter New England LHD, delivering contemporary orthopaedic services to a growing community. You'll gain valuable, practical experience in a supportive environment while enjoying the lifestyle benefits of the Hunter region.

Have more at Maitland - more opportunity, more support, more progression towards Orthopaedic SET.

You Can Have More At Maitland Hospital

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Experience and qualifications commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent clinical skills, judgement and expertise.

Ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team with demonstrated skills in time management, prioritisation and problem solving.

High level communication skills, both written and verbal with a demonstrated ability to convey information to both a clinical and non clinical audience.

Commitment to own continuing professional development and self-education with evidence of motivation to further career in orthopaedics.

Demonstrated evidence of a commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management

Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Educator
Remuneration: $60.84 - $62.82 per hour
Hours Per Week: 20
Requisition ID: REQ668580
Application close: Sunday 12th July 2026 at 11.59pm

Central Coast Local Health District (CCLHD) has an exciting opportunity for a Clinical Nurse Educator to join our Critical Care Cardiac Cath Lab team. This is a great opportunity to showcase your skills and make a real difference in the provision of services to the Central Coast Community.

About The Opportunity

As a Clinical Nurse Educator at Gosford Hospital Cardiac Cath Lab, you will be instrumental in delivering expert clinical education and training to promote competence of nursing staff.
The Clinical Nurse Educator (Critical Care - Cardiac Cath Lab) is responsible for leading, coordinating, and evaluating education and professional development activities for nursing staff within the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory and related critical care services. The role supports the delivery of safe, evidence-based, high-quality cardiovascular care through staff education, competency development, clinical leadership, and quality improvement initiatives.

In this role, you will :

Develop, implement, and evaluate education programs for nursing staff working in the Cardiac Cath Lab.

Coordinate orientation and onboarding programs for new nurses and multidisciplinary team members.

Assess, maintain, and document clinical competencies for Cath Lab nursing staff.

Provide clinical coaching, mentoring, and bedside education.

Facilitate continuing professional development activities and specialty cardiovascular education.

Support nurses undertaking postgraduate studies in critical care, cardiovascular, or perioperative specialties.

Provide expert clinical guidance 

Coordinate simulation-based education

Work closely with Nurse Unit Managers, cardiologists, interventional cardiologists, electrophysiologists, radiographers, and allied health staff.

 For more information about this role, please view the Position Description

About You

You will bring a strong commitment to high-quality community care and a passion for helping people maintain their health and dignity. You will:

Hold current registration with the Australian Health Practioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as a Registered Nurse Division 1

Hold a current drivers licence

Recent Cardiology-Critical care experience at an advanced practitioner level.

Relevant clinical or education post registration qualifications or equivalent education and clinical experience.

Demonstrated experience delivering education and understanding of learning and assessment principles.

Demonstrated knowledge and skill using technology appropriate to the clinical area.

Applicants must have current Australian work rights. We are unable to consider applicants who do not meet this requirement.

Benefits

 

At Central Coast Local Health District, you'll be supported to grow, thrive, and succeed:

Work-Life Balance

.Accrued day off each month (ADO)

.17.5% annual leave loading

.Paid parental leave

Financial Benefits

.Salary packaging to increase your take-home pay

.Novated leasing options

.Relocation assistance (where eligible)

Health & Wellbeing

.Discounted gym access through Fitness Passport

.Free flu vaccinations

.Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

.Access discounted private health insurance

Career Growth

.Access to professional development and education

.Secondment and career-advancement opportunities across the District

Need More Information?
Contact: Jordan Fenech
Phone: 4320 2843
Email: jordan.fenech@health.nsw.gov.au

Click here to find out more about applying for this position.

Working for Central Coast Local Health District - NSW Health

Central Coast Local Health District is committed to implementing the Child Safe Standards.

Central Coast Local Health District is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants can access support through the Stepping Up initiative, which provides guidance on the NSW Health recruitment process. You're also welcome to reach out to Nathan Bramston in our Aboriginal Workforce Development Team at CCLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au or call 02 4320 3519 for one-on-one support.

Vaccination Requirements

All NSW Health workers are required to comply with the Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination Against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy Directive. This includes:

Category A positions: Mandatory evidence of protection against specified infectious diseases, including annual influenza vaccination and tuberculosis assessment.

Applicants must provide appropriate evidence of compliance prior to commencement. For detailed information, please refer to the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination Policy.

NSW Health strongly recommends all workers stay up to date with COVID-19 vaccinations as per the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation guidelines. However, COVID-19 vaccination is not a condition of employment.

Additional Information

An Eligibility List (E-List) or talent pool may be created from this recruitment episode to assist in filling future permanent, temporary, or casual full-time and part-time positions.

Stay Connected

Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn to stay up to date with career opportunities and the latest updates.

You are encouraged to complete applications on a weekday where Technical Support is available Monday to Friday 8.30am to 4.30pm by phoning ROB Help Desk on 1300 679 367.    Click here to Apply now →

Position: Airconditioning and Refrigeration Mechanic
Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $95,000 - $110,000 p/a plus Super
Employer Name: Ecoplus Mechanical Services
A.B.N. 66 660 929 304
Job Location: Level 13, 60 Castlereagh Street, Sydney, NSW, 2000,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 20 Jul 2026 > 17 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1698-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client is seeking to add an experienced Airconditioning and Refrigeration Mechanic to the Ecoplus Mechanical Services team in Sydney. With decades of industry experience, Ecoplus delivers reliable HVAC and refrigeration installation, maintenance and repair services across commercial and residential environments, including offices, hospitals, schools, data centres, airports, defence facilities, high-rise properties and marine applications.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Install, commission, service and repair residential, commercial and industrial airconditioning and refrigeration systems.
- Diagnose mechanical, electrical and control faults using technical drawings, schematics and appropriate testing equipment.
- Service and maintain split, ducted, cassette, packaged and VRV/VRF airconditioning systems.
- Maintain, diagnose and repair chillers, central plant systems, fan coil units and chilled-water equipment.
- Service commercial refrigeration plant, including cool rooms, display cabinets and temperature-controlled equipment.
- Undertake preventative maintenance, scheduled servicing and reactive breakdown repairs across Sydney customer sites.
- Install and replace compressors, motors, condensers, evaporators, valves, switches, gauges and control components.
- Measure, fabricate and install refrigerant pipework, drainage, ductwork and associated mechanical components.
- Complete brazing, pressure testing, evacuation, leak detection and refrigerant charging in accordance with regulations.
- Commission new and repaired systems and undertake performance testing to confirm correct and efficient operation.
- Carry out electrical fault-finding, component testing and replacement within the authorised scope of the trade.
- Complete compressor replacements, equipment modifications, system upgrades and retrofits where required.
- Provide full lifecycle support across equipment installation, commissioning, servicing, maintenance and repair.
- Record faults, repairs, maintenance activities, refrigerant usage and commissioning results accurately.
- Communicate professionally with customers, contractors and site representatives regarding faults and required works.
- Comply with workplace safety, environmental obligations and site-specific operating requirements.
- Work independently and collaboratively with technicians, contractors and manufacturer-trained service personnel.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- A minimum of three years’ relevant experience installing, servicing and repairing airconditioning and refrigeration systems.
- An AQF Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration, or an equivalent recognised trade qualification.
- A current Refrigerant Handling Licence and any trade licences or registrations required to perform the role legally in Australia.
- A current Australian driver’s licence and the ability to travel between customer sites across the Sydney metropolitan area.
- Demonstrated experience with commercial or industrial HVAC systems, including chillers, central plant or VRV/VRF equipment.
- Demonstrated ability to diagnose mechanical, electrical and control faults and complete reliable repairs or component replacement.
- Competence in brazing, leak detection, pressure testing, evacuation, refrigerant recovery, charging and system commissioning.
- Ability to interpret technical drawings and schematics, maintain accurate service records and work safely with limited supervision.

Please include Reference: J1698-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.
